Daily Brief

The day's most consequential development is President Trump's surprise deal to import Russian diesel into the United States, a dramatic reversal of sanctions policy that drew sharp condemnation from Ukrainian President Zelensky, who called it 'a gift to Putin' [BBC, Le Monde, The Hindu]. The agreement, which suspends sanctions on Russian diesel exports through April, comes as Trump faces political pressure over fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections. Meanwhile, Hurricane Isaias made landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast as the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, forcing mass evacuations and leaving hundreds of thousands without power across Florida, Alabama, and Georgia [BBC, The Guardian, Financial Times]. The Nobel Committee awarded its Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, the South African jurist who chaired the UN commission that found Israel guilty of genocide in Gaza, a decision certain to provoke controversy [The Guardian, France 24, The Hindu]. In Kenya, health officials are racing to contain the country's first Ebola case after a patient who travelled from the DRC died in Nairobi, with 57 contacts now under surveillance [RFI]. The Trump administration also escalated its confrontation with international institutions, announcing sanctions on the International Criminal Court and suspending major IT firms including Cognizant, Infosys, and Microsoft from the US green card programme [Le Monde, Nikkei Asia, The Hindu].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Trump Announces Russian Diesel Import Deal, Suspending Sanctions as Ukraine Condemns 'Gift to Putin'

  • President Trump announced a deal with Putin to import 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel immediately, with 500,000 more tonnes in November and potentially millions more to follow
  • The US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7, 2026, though other Russian assets in American banks remain frozen
  • Ukrainian President Zelensky condemned the deal as 'an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged' and called for stronger US pressure on Russia
  • Russian strikes killed at least 11 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region the day after the deal was announced, including three children

02 Climate

Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall in Florida as First Atlantic Hurricane of 2026 Season

  • Hurricane Isaias struck Florida's northern Gulf Coast Friday night with 80mph winds, the latest first hurricane of the season since 1905 due to El Niño conditions
  • Hundreds of thousands of households in Florida, Alabama, and Georgia lost power; all three states declared states of emergency
  • Mandatory evacuations were ordered for coastal communities in Florida and for non-residents in key Alabama counties
  • Oil and gas production has been disrupted across the Gulf region as the storm system moves inland

03 Society

South African Jurist Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize for Promoting International Law

  • The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, 85, citing her commitment to universal legal principles and holding states accountable
  • Pillay chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza and that Netanyahu, Herzog, and Gallant incited genocide
  • She served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, on the International Criminal Tribunal, and currently sits as a judge at the International Court of Justice
  • Israel rejected her commission's findings as biased and refused to cooperate with its investigation

04 Society

Kenya Races to Contain First Ebola Case After Patient Dies Following Travel from DRC

  • Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case after a Kenyan man who lived in the DRC for seven years died on October 5 after travelling through Uganda to Nairobi
  • The patient tested positive for Bundibugyo Ebola at Kenya's National Virology Reference Laboratory; symptoms included fever, bleeding beneath the skin, and painful swallowing
  • Health authorities have identified 57 contacts, 10 of whom are being closely monitored for symptoms
  • The case has exposed failures in border screening processes across three countries

05 Policy

US Suspends Major IT Firms Including Cognizant, Infosys, Microsoft from Green Card Programme

  • The US Department of Labour suspended Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft, and Adobe from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme
  • The suspension blocks new applications and processing of pending permanent labour certifications involving these companies
  • Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling stated these companies have requested almost three million foreign workers since 2009 and received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals
  • Vice-President J.D. Vance, head of the US Anti-Fraud Task Force, was present at the announcement
